title: Proton pump inhibitor use and the risk of chronic kidney disease
authors: Lazarus B, Chen Y, Wilson FP, Sang Y, Chang AR, Coresh J, et al.
followUp: median 13.9 years; replication cohort median 6.2 years
population: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) participants with eGFR of at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 from 1996 to 1999; replication in 248,751 Geisinger Health System patients
funder: The ARIC study is supported by National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute contracts HHSN268201100005C to HHSN268201100012C; M. E. Grams receives support from the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (K08DK092287). Some data were supplied by the United States Renal Data System.
authorConflicts: Not shown in the PMC author manuscript.
result: ARIC: incident chronic kidney disease in 56 of 322 baseline PPI users (14.2 per 1000 person-years) and 1382 of 10,160 non-users (10.7 per 1000 person-years); adjusted HR 1.50 (95% CI 1.14 to 1.96); 10-year absolute risk 11.8% against an expected 8.5% without PPI (difference 3.3 percentage points). Replication: adjusted HR 1.17 (1.12 to 1.23); 10-year risk 15.6% against 13.9%. PPI users were more often obese and taking antihypertensive drugs; the authors state that the observational design does not establish causality.
